correctness.rationale: On each ordered smooth sector, Birkhoff--James orthogonality is equivalent to annihilation by the unique norming functional. For x_t=(1,t), differentiation gives the unique orthogonal direction y_t=(omega t^(q-1),-1). Because 0<omega<=1 and 0<t<1, y_t lies in the opposite ordered smooth sector, where the reverse functional equation is omega(omega t^(q-1))^(q-1)=t. This is exactly omega^q t^(q(q-2))=1. The three q-regimes are then exhaustive, and every non-Euclidean parameter pair admits a one-way orthogonal pair; the sole remaining parameter (omega,q)=(1,2) is Euclidean and hence Radon.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification inside a classical two-parameter family: it identifies exactly when Lorentz geometry has the defining reciprocity property of Radon planes and, more strongly, gives the full smooth-sector reciprocity locus by one explicit equation. Radon symmetry is a structural property of normed planes tied to duality and Minkowski geometry, so the result is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known scalar constant.
